SHAPE AND NATIVE: the card's decision is direct-driver and the package is a direct decorated Driver. native is ueye:camera, one of the card's two override entry symbols; the class carries the SDK surface directly (SetImageSize, SetImagePos, CaptureVideo, StopLiveVideo, Exposure, SaveImage, ExitCamera), while pycam only wraps a camera in its cam attribute and forwards snapshot (ueye.py:118-132). No hardware factory is shipped and driver.lock.json backends is only {"fake": ".fake:FakeUEyeCamera"}: the clone cannot be imported by the Python 3 runtime, the gate never touches hardware, and the blocked status means no hardware path is claimed.

COVERED: reads width, height, image_x and image_y from the SDK query codes through SetImageSize and SetImagePos; writes the same four AOI fields (operator_required); cap.sensing.image.v1 capture with optional width, height and exposure_ms inputs, following the clone's snapshot sequence CaptureVideo(wait=IS.WAIT), StopLiveVideo(wait=IS.WAIT), SaveImage(path) (ueye.py:128-132); the @estop calls ExitCamera (ueye.py:509-511) and the safe state is the closed camera. The fake implements only the upstream camera methods and keeps its own AOI state; every number in fake.py is marked # placeholder. The fake's SaveImage writes a 1 x 1 BMP placeholder, not a frame; the action reports the camera's current AOI width and height, while on hardware the saved file would hold whatever the active image memory holds. The package ships no hardware backend and does not drive the image-memory allocation and activation that pycam performs at ueye.py:122-123.

LIMITS: width, height, image_x, image_y and the capture inputs width, height and exposure_ms are Limit.operator_required. No text file of the clone states a pixel, position, sensor or exposure range: SetImageSize says the size range is queried from the installed camera with IS.GET_IMAGE_SIZE_X_MIN/MAX/INC and Y_MIN/MAX/INC (ueye.py:348-357), SetImagePos forwards two integers (ueye.py:453-457), and Exposure only says it sets the time in ms (ueye.py:542-544). The constructor defaults 1024 x 768 (ueye.py:146-149) are not used as bounds. site-limits.example.json is an example operator overlay with example ranges, not a fact about any camera; until an operator supplies real bounds every write and every bounded capture input is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET.

SAFETY: the effective risk is R1, above the card's R0 floor, because the bound cap.device.configure.v1 class is R1; the capture class cap.sensing.image.v1 is R0. The e-stop is the native ExitCamera and the safe state is the closed camera; no independent hardware e-stop is claimed and no physical protection is claimed. No hardware was attached and no hardware backend was run.

NOT COVERED: the pixel array itself (the receipt carries a BMP path and the AOI size, not the pixels; the fake writes a 1 x 1 placeholder); the image-memory allocation and activation (AllocImageMem/SetImageMem) that pycam performs at ueye.py:122-123, so a future hardware factory would have to allocate the buffer before CaptureVideo; an exposure readback (the clone exposes only the Exposure setter, so the capture action applies exposure_ms but cannot report the stored value); the EEPROM, ring-buffer/sequence, color-mode, subsampling and FreezeVideo methods; the pycam convenience wrapper; and any MHS-Device-level evidence.
